title: Complete Food Container Guide: Plastic, Stainless Steel, and Glass
excerpt: Complete guide to choosing the best food containers from various materials - BPA-free plastic, stainless steel, and glass. Price comparisons, pros and cons, and food storage tips.
content: Choosing the right **food container** is more than just storing leftovers - it's about protecting your family's health, reducing food waste, and saving on your monthly expenses. Quality food containers can extend food shelf life by 3-5 times longer compared to ordinary containers.
Our team at Sesoris has noticed that the happiest customers aren't those with the largest homes, but those with the most consistent organization habits.
![Various types of food containers made from plastic, stainless steel, and glass arranged neatly](/images/blog/wadah-makanan-hero.webp)

This article provides an in-depth discussion of three main **food container** materials - BPA-free plastic, stainless steel, and glass - complete with price comparisons, advantages and disadvantages of each, and a guide to choosing the most suitable option for your needs.

> **Key Takeaways:**
> - Choose products with clear safety labels (food-grade, BPA-free) for daily use
> - Investing slightly more in quality materials (glass, grade 304 stainless steel) saves long-term costs
> - Match sizes to family needs, neither too large nor too small
> - Local marketplaces like Tokopedia, Shopee, and [Sesoris](https://www.sesoris.com/) offer competitive prices with maintained quality
## Why Choosing the Right Food Container Matters?

Many people still use whatever food containers they have on hand - thin plastic bags, leftover ice cream containers, or even reused plastic wrap. This habit not only causes food to spoil quickly, but can also pose health risks due to chemical migration from the container to the food. For additional information, also see the guide from [The Spruce](https://www.thespruce.com/).
Quality **food containers** offer several important benefits:
- **Airtight sealing** - prevents bacteria and moisture from entering, keeping food fresher longer
- **Food-grade material** - safe for direct contact with food without contamination risk
- **Temperature resistant** - can be used for freezer storage and microwave heating
- **Cost-effective** - reducing food waste means saving on your grocery bill
## BPA-Free Plastic Food Containers

Plastic is the most widely used material for **food containers** because it's affordable and lightweight. However, not all plastics are safe for food. Make sure you choose containers labeled BPA-free with food-grade certification. For additional information, also see the guide from [Real Simple](https://www.realsimple.com/).
### Types of Plastic Safe for Food
Check the recycling triangle symbol at the bottom of the container. The number inside indicates the type of plastic used:
| Code | Plastic Type | Safe for Food? | Heat Resistant | Notes |
| 1 (PET) | Polyethylene Terephthalate | One-time use only | Low | Mineral water bottles |
| 2 (HDPE) | High-Density Polyethylene | Yes | Medium | Milk bottles, water jugs |
| 3 (PVC) | Polyvinyl Chloride | No | Low | Avoid for food |
| 4 (LDPE) | Low-Density Polyethylene | Yes | Low | Plastic wrap, bags |
| 5 (PP) | Polypropylene | Yes, best choice | High (248°F) | Food containers, microwave-safe |
| 6 (PS) | Polystyrene | Not recommended | Low | Styrofoam |
| 7 (Other) | Mixed/Tritan | Check BPA-Free label | Varies | Includes premium Tritan |
### Advantages of Plastic Containers
- Lightweight and shatter-proof, perfect for travel and school lunch boxes
- Most affordable compared to other materials
- Available in countless sizes and shapes
- Easy to stack and doesn't take up much storage space
- Some are microwave-safe, especially PP and Tritan
### Disadvantages of Plastic Containers
- Can discolor if storing coconut-based dishes, turmeric, or deeply colored foods
- Absorbs food odors, especially from strongly spiced dishes like rendang
- Shorter lifespan compared to glass or stainless steel (1-3 years)
- Surface easily scratches and becomes a breeding ground for bacteria
## Stainless Steel Food Containers

Stainless steel is becoming increasingly popular as a **food container** material due to its exceptional durability and high food safety standards. This material doesn't react with food, doesn't absorb odors, and can last for decades.
### Types of Stainless Steel for Food Containers
- **Stainless 304 (18/8)** - the most common food-safe grade. Corrosion resistant and easy to clean
- **Stainless 316** - premium grade with better corrosion resistance, commonly used in professional food service
### When to Choose Stainless Steel?
- **School lunch boxes** - durable and won't shatter if dropped from a table
- **Dry food storage** - rice, beans, and snacks stay crispy thanks to airtight sealing
- **Camping and outdoor activities** - lighter than glass and withstands all weather conditions
- **Daily meal prep** - easy to clean and doesn't retain food odors from previous meals
### Stainless Steel Limitations

Cannot be used in the microwave due to the metal material. Food contents aren't visible from outside so containers need labels. Initial cost is higher than plastic, though it's more economical long-term since replacement isn't needed frequently.
## Glass Food Containers

Glass is a premium choice for **food containers** that prioritizes safety and cleanliness. There's no risk of chemical migration, it doesn't absorb odors, and the transparent appearance makes it easy to identify contents without opening the lid.
### Types of Glass for Food Containers
1. **Borosilicate glass** - resists extreme temperatures from -4°F to 752°F. Can go directly from freezer to oven without risk of cracking. Best choice for intensive use
2. **Tempered glass** - stronger than regular glass and resistant to light impacts. More affordable than borosilicate but with a more limited temperature range
3. **Soda lime glass** - standard glass that's cheaper but not suitable for drastic temperature changes. Good only for room temperature storage
### Advantages of Glass Containers
- Doesn't absorb odors, colors, or flavors from any food
- Transparent so contents are clearly visible without opening the lid
- Safe for microwave, oven, freezer, and dishwasher (borosilicate)
- Doesn't release chemicals into food under any conditions
- Elegant appearance and can be served directly at the dining table
### Disadvantages of Glass Containers
- Heavier than plastic and stainless steel
- Risk of breaking if dropped, especially soda lime glass
- Higher price, especially for borosilicate glass
- Not suitable for long-distance travel due to breakage risk and weight
## Complete Comparison of Three Materials
Here's a comprehensive comparison to help you choose the **food container** that best suits your needs:
| Aspect | BPA-Free Plastic | Stainless Steel | Borosilicate Glass |
| Weight | Very light | Light-medium | Heavy |
| Heat resistance | Medium (PP: 248°F) | High | Very high (752°F) |
| Microwave safe | Yes (PP, Tritan) | No | Yes |
| Odor absorption | Yes, especially strong spices | No | No |
| Lifespan | 1-3 years | 10-20+ years | 5-15 years |
| Food safety | Good (if food-grade) | Very good | Very good |
| Eco-friendly | Less | Very good | Good |
| Best for | Light lunch boxes, everyday use | School lunch boxes, outdoor | Meal prep, refrigerator storage |
## Food Container Size Guide
Choosing the right size is just as important as choosing the material. Here's a size guide based on needs:
| Size | Best For | Serving | Example Use |
| 150-300 ml | Sauces, condiments, spices | 1-2 small servings | Salad dressing, jam, sambal |
| 400-750 ml | Side dishes, snacks | 1-2 servings | Work lunch, individual meal prep |
| 1-1.5 liters | Rice, soup, main dishes | 2-3 servings | Family dinner, small meal prep |
| 2-3 liters | Batch cooking | 4-6 servings | Weekly meal prep, catering |
| 3.5 liters and up | Raw ingredient storage | Bulk | Rice, flour, legumes |
For a family of 4 doing weekly meal prep, you ideally need 8-12 containers sized 500ml-1.5L and 4-6 small containers for sauces and condiments.

## Tips for Proper Food Storage
Even the best **food container** won't be effective if stored incorrectly. Here are tips to keep your food fresh longer:
### In the Refrigerator
- Cool food to room temperature before putting it in the refrigerator to avoid condensation inside the container
- Store cooked food on upper shelves, raw ingredients on lower shelves to prevent cross-contamination
- Label each container with the date so you know when to eat it before it spoils
### In the Freezer
- Leave about 0.8 inches of space from the lid since food expands when frozen
- Use containers labeled freezer-safe to prevent cracking from extreme temperatures
- Food can last 1-3 months in the freezer depending on the type
### At Room Temperature
- Only for dry foods like rice, flour, legumes, and snacks
- Make sure containers are completely airtight to prevent insects and moisture
- Store in a cool place away from direct sunlight
## How to Maintain Food Containers for Longevity
Proper care significantly extends the lifespan of your **food containers**:
- **Plastic** - hand wash using a soft sponge. Soak with baking soda to remove stubborn stains and odors from rendang or turmeric
- **Stainless steel** - wash with regular soap and warm water. For stubborn stains, use a mixture of vinegar and baking soda
- **Glass** - can be washed in the dishwasher or by hand. Avoid sudden temperature changes on non-borosilicate glass
- **Rubber seals** - remove and wash separately each time you wash the container. Dry completely before reattaching. Replace every 1-2 years if starting to harden
- **Store without lids** when not in use to allow good air circulation inside the container and prevent musty odors
## Food Container Recommendations for Various Needs
### For Weekly Meal Prep

Choose a set of glass food containers in uniform sizes so they stack easily in the refrigerator. Glass is recommended because you can reheat directly in the microwave without transferring containers, saving time and dishes.
### For School Lunch Boxes
Stainless steel containers are the best choice for school lunch boxes because they're shatter-proof and extremely durable. Choose ones with dividers so rice, main dishes, and vegetables don't mix.
### For Home-Based Food Business
If you sell food, consider containers that are food-grade, leak-proof, and look professional. Attractive PP plastic containers can make a good impression on customers.
### For Freezer Storage
Make sure containers are labeled freezer-safe. Borosilicate glass and PP plastic are safe for freezing. Leave 0.4-0.8 inches of empty space from the lid since food liquids expand when frozen.
## Conclusion

There's no single perfect **food container** material for every situation. The best approach is to have a combination - glass containers for meal prep and home storage, stainless steel for on-the-go lunch boxes, and BPA-free plastic for lightweight everyday use.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Here are answers to the most frequently asked reader questions on this topic.
**Q: How long do quality home organization products typically last?**

With proper routine care, food-grade plastic products last 3-5 years, while borosilicate glass and grade 304 stainless steel can last 10+ years. Key factors are consistent maintenance and avoiding extreme temperature exposure.
**Q: Is this product food-safe?**

Ensure the product is labeled "food-grade" or "BPA-free" before using it for food storage. Safe materials include borosilicate glass, grade 304 stainless steel, and certified food-grade plastic. Avoid plastic without food safety certification, especially for hot or oily foods.
**Q: How do I clean and maintain it?**

Wash with mild dish soap and warm water. Avoid abrasive sponges that can scratch the surface. For stubborn stains, use a baking soda and water paste as a natural cleaner. Dry completely before storing to prevent mold and bacteria.
**Q: What is the price difference between local and imported products?**

Local Indonesian products are typically 30-50% more affordable than imports of similar quality. For daily home organization needs, local products meet the standard. Consider imports only if you need specific features not available in the local market.
